claims.text: A residency license converts to an initial or continuing professional license only if the applicant meets the requirements for an IPL (LICN-020) or CPL (LICN-024) and is recommended by the EPP that prepared the licensee.

question: Teacher has a CPL expiring in 3 months and has 6.5 CEUs from this cycle, 1.0 of them in digital learning. Enough to renew?

input.query: Teacher has a CPL expiring in 3 months and has 6.5 CEUs from this cycle, 1.0 of them in digital learning. Enough to renew?

answer.summary: As stated, 6.5 CEUs does not meet the 8 CEUs required for a teacher's CPL renewal in either grade band, so the teacher is 1.5 CEUs short. The renewal could still succeed only if an exemption applies (such as National Board Certification or General Assembly membership) or if the teacher earns the missing CEUs and meets the evaluation requirement.

claims.text: A teacher holding a CPL must renew that license every five years.
Teachers in Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 5 must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle: three in the license area, three related to literacy, and two general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment.
Teachers in Grades 6 through 12 must complete eight CEUs per renewal cycle: four in the license area and four general CEUs germane to the K-12 environment.
One CEU equals either two-thirds of a semester credit hour from an institution of higher education or ten clock hours of professional development programming.
Arithmetic: the requirement is 8 CEUs and the teacher has 6.5 CEUs, so the shortfall is 8 - 6.5 = 1.5 CEUs. This shortfall is the same in either grade band because the total is 8 in both.

The passages do not list digital learning as a CEU category. Sources of CEUs are college or university credit and professional development programs. Whether the 1.0 digital learning CEU counts toward the general or license-area categories cannot be determined from the passages, and the general-category and license-area minimums must be met separately.

A teacher who receives National Board Certification in the renewal cycle receives credit for all eight CEUs for that cycle. A teacher who renews National Board Certification receives credit for two CEUs for that cycle.
A member of the General Assembly is exempt from the CEU requirements during any renewal cycle in which the member serves, if the member notifies DPI of the exemption during that cycle.

Mandatory training hours count toward CEUs only if the training is required by State law or by a local board of education as a condition of employment, and the educator has otherwise met the renewal requirements.

To renew a CPL, a teacher employed by a local board of education must have evidence of a rating of at least proficient on the most recent annual evaluation, defined as Proficient or higher on three of the five NC Professional Teaching Standards including Proficient on Standard 4.

If a teacher employed by a local board is in the final year of a renewal cycle and was not deemed proficient, the LSAU may place the teacher on a mandatory improvement plan. If placed and the teacher otherwise meets licensure requirements, DPI issues an IPL. The policy's expiration rule is written for a teacher who meets the Section 1 criteria but is not placed on a plan, and it does not address a teacher who is short on CEUs.
Every license expires on June 30 of the calendar year in which it is set to expire, unless it is renewed, extended, or converted under SBE policy.

question: Teacher is a former military educator with 8 years experience teaching in DoD schools, no NC license. Which NC license applies?

input.query: Teacher is a former military educator with 8 years experience teaching in DoD schools, no NC license. Which NC license applies?

answer.summary: The passages cannot name one license yet. The answer depends on whether the teacher holds a clear out-of-state license, how many years of licensed teaching experience they have, whether they completed an educator preparation program, and whether they are on active duty or the spouse of an active-duty servicemember. Their 8 years of experience is more than the 3-year threshold that the initial-license route for out-of-state applicants uses, so that route likely does not apply.

claims.text: For an out-of-state applicant with fewer than three years of licensed professional educator experience, an IPL may be issued if the applicant holds a license in the corresponding area in another jurisdiction, or completed an educator preparation program recognized by the jurisdiction where it is based.
An applicant with a clear out-of-state license and fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience in that jurisdiction may also qualify for an IPL under the initial professional license rule.

An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for a CPL only if they hold a clear license from another jurisdiction and either hold NBPTS certification or the other jurisdiction's requirements were substantially similar to North Carolina's, meaning completion of a recognized EPP and a passing score on an out-of-state exam for each license area sought.
A clear license must be in good standing, renewable by the issuing authority, and free of revocation, discipline, and pending or surrendered investigations for unprofessional conduct.
Out-of-state exam results must be presented at the time of initial NC licensure, and an out-of-state applicant may not use those results to convert an IPL to a CPL.

A jurisdiction is defined as a state, territory, or federal district of the United States, or a foreign country or political subdivision. The passages do not say whether a DoD school system counts as a jurisdiction, so it is unclear whether DoD teaching experience counts as licensed experience under these rules.

Under the Continuing Professional License rule, the three-year licensed teaching experience requirement and the Beginning Teacher Support Program exemption for at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina both apply to CPL applicants who hold an NC IPL or residency license. This rule does not directly govern an applicant with no NC license.

If the applicant is on active duty or is the spouse of an active-duty servicemember and relocated under military orders, the special provisions for servicemembers and spouses apply. Recognition of a covered out-of-state license is available only if the license is in good standing and not under discipline or investigation. Those provisions do not cover former servicemembers.

A residency license requires that the applicant meet G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(5) and have either completed 24 hours of coursework in the content area or passed the applicable licensure examination for that area. A Residency license is a one-year license renewable twice, and it applies only to applicants under employment with a public school unit requesting it.

A permit to teach requires at least a bachelor's degree and that the person has never held any other North Carolina professional educator license. It is valid only until June 30 of the fiscal year requested and cannot be renewed.

Military instructional experience may earn salary experience credit of one full year for every two years of full-time instructional duties on active military duty. This applies only to veterans first employed by an NC LEA on or after July 1, 2014, and only for active-duty service, so it may not cover DoD civilian school teaching. It affects salary credit, not license type.

Non-teaching military leadership experience can also earn salary credit, but only for commissioned officers, warrant officers, and non-commissioned officers who completed a sanctioned military leadership course. This also affects salary credit, not license type.

claims.text: Welding is listed as a Trade and Industrial Education license area within Career and Technical Education.

An applicant with a high school diploma (or equivalent) or associate's degree (V-Level) may be issued a teaching license in Career and Technical Education, provided the applicant meets all other requirements for the license classification sought, as provided in Section 5.

The general rule requires completion of an educator preparation program at the Bachelor's (A), Master's (M), Specialist (S), or Doctoral (D) level, so the high school or associate's pathway is an exception to that general rule.

Each teacher license is classified by the applicant's qualifications, with options including Initial Professional, Continuing Professional, Residency, Limited, Permit to Teach, Emergency, International Faculty, Lifetime, and Provisional licenses.

The passages do not define that required training or work experience.

Non-teaching work experience counts for salary purposes only if it is at least half-time (20 hours or more per week), was completed after age 18, did not include on-the-job training, was paid and documented, and is directly related to the area of licensure, as recommended by the employing public school unit.

Relevant non-teaching experience is judged on alignment with the Standard Course of Study content standards and on transferable skills, and credit does not transfer to licensure areas for which the experience is not relevant.

Experience credit for non-teaching work is measured in years of full-time work (one year for every year after a bachelor's degree, or one year for every two years before). The passages give no conversion from hours to years, so 5000 hours cannot be converted to years of credit from these passages.

The license indicates the grade levels, content areas, specializations, years of experience, and highest degree level for which the applicant is eligible. Degree level is based on the highest degree from an educator preparation program.

The passages do not say whether an industry credential in welding meets any CTE license requirement, and the test table in LICN-003 shown in the passages does not list a Trade and Industrial welding test.

question: What's the difference between an IPL and a CPL in NC?

input.query: What's the difference between an IPL and a CPL in NC?

answer.summary: An IPL is a three-year, nonrenewable license, and a CPL is a five-year, renewable license; both let the holder practice as an independent professional educator in North Carolina. A CPL requires more to obtain, including examination requirements, at least three years of licensed teaching experience, and for teachers a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless an exception applies.

claims.text: An initial professional license (IPL) is a three-year, nonrenewable license issued to an applicant or professional educator who meets the relevant SBE policy requirements.
A continuing professional license (CPL) is a five-year, renewable license issued to an applicant or professional educator who meets the relevant SBE policy requirements.
Both an IPL and a CPL entitle the licensee to practice as an independent professional educator in North Carolina.

To qualify for an IPL, an applicant generally must complete a recognized North Carolina educator preparation program (EPP) and be recommended by it, complete an out-of-state EPP, or hold a clear out-of-state license and have fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience in that jurisdiction.

To qualify for a CPL as a teacher, an applicant must hold an IPL or residency license in North Carolina, satisfy the applicable licensure examination requirements before or during the third year of licensure, have at least three years of licensed teaching experience, and complete a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless an exception applies.

Exceptions to the Beginning Teacher Support Program requirement for a CPL include at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina, or having previously held a CPL that reverted to an IPL under LICN-030.

For administrators and student services personnel, a CPL requires satisfying the applicable licensure examination requirements before or during the third year of licensure and meeting the other requirements in LICN-011 or LICN-012.
A teacher employed by a local board of education must have evidence of at least a "proficient" rating on the most recent annual evaluation in NCEES to renew a CPL.
If a teacher's CPL reverts to an IPL under a mandatory improvement plan, the teacher's license is reissued as an IPL, and the reversion is not a demotion or salary reduction.
An out-of-state applicant may not use out-of-state exam results to convert an IPL to a CPL.
A CPL remains in effect for five years after the licensee retires from full-time employment as a professional educator.
